title: Contractual SSO assertions and tiered RBAC commitments — pricing/packaging experiment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Evaluate contract language and packaging options for SSO (SAML + OIDC) and role-based access controls (RBAC) so we can reduce sales friction while preserving legal/operational guardrails. This ticket defines an experiment that tests two packaging models (enterprise-included vs. modular add-on) and a set of explicit contractual commitments (assertion guarantees, SCIM/SCIM provisioning timelines, admin role mapping support, audit retention). Goal is to surface revenue impact, legal risk, and implementation effort before we standardize wording in the contract templates and Security Questionnaire answers.
goals: Reduce SOC/Procurement objection rate on SSO/RBAC from enterprise prospects by 30% in 90 days
Determine price elasticity for including SSO/RBAC in enterprise tier vs as a paid add-on
Agree on contract-level commitments (assertion properties, provisioning SLA, role mapping support, audit log retention) that Legal and Security can sign off
Produce concrete guidance for Sales playbook and CLA/contract clauses for inclusion in term sheets
proposed_packaging: Option A - Enterprise Included: SSO (SAML/OIDC) + RBAC base features included in enterprise plans; premium role mapping and 1:1 onboarding as consulting add-on
Option B - Modular Add-on: Base product sold separately; SSO connector and RBAC enterprise features sold as a named add-on SKU with clear pricing bands
Hybrid - Entitlement Tiering: Core SSO (single-idp, 10 groups) included; advanced SAML features (multiple IDPs, signed assertions, audience binding) and SCIM provisioning as paid tier
Pilot Offer: Waive SSO add-on for first 3 months for customers committing to 12-month dedicated capacity contracts
contract_commitments: Assertion guarantees: Affirmation that issued SAML/OIDC assertions will contain nameID, email, groups when requested (where technically available)
Signed assertions & audience binding: Optional feature; if included in contract, we commit to maintaining cert rotation and documented validation steps
SCIM provisioning SLA: Initial provisioning connector delivery within 10 business days for standard IdPs; 20 business days for custom integrations (when purchased as onboarding service)
RBAC mapping: Provide a mapping template and support up to 50 role templates; above that level, scope as professional services
Audit logs: Contractual retention of authentication events for 90 days by default, 365 days as premium add-on
Security incident response: Standard enterprise SLA for authentication-impacting incidents (initial response within 2 hours, full remediation plan within 72 hours)
experiment_design: Run a 6-week pilot with 12 inbound enterprise opportunities: split evenly between Option A and Option B offers
Sales playbook A/B: Provide two term sheets to SDR/AE teams with identical pricing except for SSO/RBAC inclusion, collect feedback and objection reasons
Legal checklist: Use two sets of contract language (concise commitments vs. expanded assertions) and route through Legal/Security review in parallel
Measure downstream operational burden by tracking implementation tickets created in ENG and time-to-provision (target < 10 business days for standard cases)
Survey procurement/security reviewers post-evaluation to capture friction points and requested changes
success_metrics: Deal close rate delta between A and B >= 8% in favor of the cheaper option for customers under $100k ARR
Average time-to-provision (for standard connectors) <= 10 business days in 80% of pilot cases
Reduction in procurement questionnaire follow-ups about SSO/RBAC from baseline by 30%
Legal sign-off on standard clause language with at most one elevated legal redline per contract in pilot group
tradeoffs_and_risks: Including SSO/RBAC in base enterprise tier increases technical support and onboarding costs; may compress margin on large deals
Selling as add-on risks longer procurement cycles but preserves unit economics
Hard contractual guarantees (e.g., assertion fields) may require additional QA and testing matrix across IdPs
Promising SCIM/connector timelines could create delivery backlog for ENG if not scoped into Dedicated onboarding roadmap
stakeholder_feedback: Sales (J. Rivera): Prefers Enterprise Included for simpler pricing and faster close on mid-market logos
Legal (M. OE2Brien): Requests explicit escape clauses for unsupported IdP attribute contracts and force majeur language around third-party IdP behavior
Security (R. Chen): Wants default audit retention to be configurable and a documented data flow diagram attached to contract addendum
Customer Success (L. Gupta): Recommends a 2-hour onboarding window option for high-velocity customers as part of pilot

notes_for_legal: Avoid absolute language around attribute availability; prefer 'to the extent provided by the customer's IdP'
Define SLAs in business days and include force majeure for third-party IdP outages
Include a simple amendment path for additional audit retention or provisioning work
